title: Sparse Authorization Index (SAI) and SIEM Adaptor: rollout & design notes
content:
Executive summary:

This doc describes the Sparse Authorization Index (SAI) design and the SIEM adaptor pattern we intend to ship as part of the RBAC v2 rollout. SAI is a compact, time-aware index that accelerates authorization lookups and provides canonical evidence pointers for SIEM export and forensic audits. The accompanying SIEM Adaptor standardizes event shaping, evidence fetch orchestration, and backpressure-safe exports to Splunk/Datadog/DF (or partner SIEMs).

Goals:
- Reduce auth latency on hot paths by moving from large entitlement graph traversals to a small read-optimized index for common checks.
- Produce deterministic, minimal audit payloads with strong evidence references for compliance and investigations.
- Provide a safe, observable migration path from current permission surface to RBAC v2 with automated discrepancy sampling and rollback hooks.

Design overview: Sparse Authorization Index (SAI)
- What SAI is: a per-principal, per-session compact index containing the active entitlements (roles, capability flags, resource selectors) plus metadata needed for verification: index_version, effective_from, effective_to (optional), provenance_id (source: git/atlas/attester), and evidence_ref (immutable pointer to archived attestation bundle).
- Why 'sparse': SAI stores only active and frequently-queried entitlements rather than the full entitlement graph. Less data -> faster lookups, fewer cache misses, simpler invalidation rules.
- Key properties: idempotent lookups, append-only index_versioning, cryptographic attestation references, timebound grants, and coarse-grained fallbacks when the index is stale.

SAI entry (example, illustrative text-only):
- principal_id: user:alice@example.com
- index_version: 2026-03-01T14:23:11Z
- entries: [role:billing-admin, resource_selector:org:acme/*, flags:{can_read_invoices:true}]
- effective_from: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z
- effective_to: 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z (optional)
- provenance_id: attestation-0a7c2
- evidence_ref: s3://audit-archive/attestations/2026/attestation-0a7c2.sig

Index lifecycle and consistency model:
- Indexes are generated by the attestation pipeline and updated incrementally. Each update increments index_version (time-based, RFC3339).
- Invalidation: index entries expire at effective_to or when a matching revocation attestation is produced.
- Read path: runtime attempts SAI lookup first (fast cache); on miss or stale, falls back to entitlement-graph evaluation. When fallback occurs, the system records a discrepancy sample event (see sampling policy below).

Evidence automation and attestation pipeline (high-level):
- Collector: listens to identity provider events, admin UI changes, SCIM syncs, and deployment hooks.
- Composer: synthesizes an attestation bundle describing the change, signs it (HSM/KMS), and writes to an immutable archive (S3/GCS with object-lock).
- Indexer: consumes approved attestation bundles and updates SAI entries atomically.
- Verifier: provides APIs that verify attestation signatures and fetch canonical evidence when telemetry or auditors request it.

Audit log schema recommendations (fields to include in every auth-related event):
- timestamp (RFC3339)
- event_id (uuid)
- actor_id (principal who triggered the action)
- request_id (trace id)
- action (authorization check e.g. read:invoice)
- resource (canonical resource id)
- result (allow | deny | fallback-allow | fallback-deny)
- auth_index_version (SAI index_version used or 'graph-v2' if fallback)
- evidence_ref (pointer to attestation bundle for the decision)
- mismatch_flag (true if runtime result differs from legacy graph result during migration sampling)
- latency_ms (authorization decision time)
- failure_reason (optional, human-readable)

SIEM Adaptor responsibilities and behavior:
- Shape: transform internal audit schema to customer SIEM format (timestamps, json flattening, field mapping). Keep payloads small by sending evidence_ref instead of embedding bundles.
- Enrichment: add context (org_id, account_tier, deploy_region) using a configurable enrichment pipeline; do not enrich with PII unless explicit opt-in and masking rules applied.
- Batching & backpressure: the adaptor blocks/queues with exponential backoff, drops non-critical sampling events when sustained backpressure occurs, and always prioritize high-fidelity 'investigation' events.
- Redaction & privacy: PII fields must be redacted or hashed per PII policy. Evidence bundles must reference object storage with access controls; the SIEM payload contains only an access-limited evidence_ref and hash.

Migration and rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0: PoC and unit-testing (2–4 weeks)
- Build SAI proof-of-concept for 1 internal service (payments-console).
- Validate attestation producer + signer flow in staging.
- Deliver lightweight dashboard showing SAI hits, misses, auth latency.

Phase 1: Internal pilot (4–6 weeks)
- Enable SAI for 3 internal teams (payments, billing, telemetry) behind feature flags.
- Run sampling: evaluate fallback discrepancies (capture both SAI and legacy-graph decisions).
- Success criteria: discrepancy rate <0.05% for allow/deny, avg auth latency improvement >= 25% for targeted endpoints.

Phase 2: Customer canary (8–12 weeks)
- Offer SAI as opt-in for a small cohort of production customers (low-risk orgs).
- Enable SIEM adaptor export in 'dry-run' mode where SIEM receives shaped events but no PII blobs.
- Monitor mismatch rates and evidence retrieval latency; iterate.

Phase 3: Gradual org-wide rollout (3 months)
- Ramp opt-ins and convert more routes to SAI-first.
- Set automated rollback triggers: if mismatch_rate > 0.2% for 1h or auth_error_rate > 0.1% for 10m then auto-failover to legacy graph for affected routes.

Phase 4: General availability (GA)
- Disable dry-run, enable SAI by default with feature-flagged overrides for customers that require classic-mode.
- Provide migration report to customers mapping historical decisions to SAI decisions for audit.

Sampling policy and discrepancy analysis:
- Always capture a sample of fallback decisions when graph != SAI; sample rate configurable but default 0.5% of fallback events, with 100% capture for admin-scoped actions.
- Discrepancy alerting: run nightly batch that computes false-deny and false-allow rates; if false-deny > 0.05% over 24h raise P0 to SRE/SEC.

Operational playbooks and runbooks (summary):
- Auth decision takes unusually long (>500ms): check SAI cache health, KVS latency, fallback counts, and SAI indexer lag.
- Evidence fetch fail: create incident, mark related events as 'evidence-missing' and fallback to graph. Use the Verifier to re-sign/rehydrate if the orig archive is intact.
- SIEM export lag: pause non-critical sample events, throttle adaptor, increase batch window; notify security ops.

Metrics to track (dashboard suggestions):
- auth.latency.p50/p95 by route
- sai.lookup.hit_rate (per route)
- sai.indexer.lag_seconds
- auth.discrepancy.rate_by_role
- siem.export.lag_seconds and siem.adaptor.queue_depth
- evidence.fetch.success_rate

Security & compliance considerations:
- Attestations must be signed with company KMS/HSM and stored in WORM-backed object store for audit retention windows (SOC2, GDPR obligations).
- Evidence_ref must embed minimal access tokens (short TTL) for SIEM-on-demand investigations; long-term references should require internal request flow.
- PII must be redacted before SIEM export unless the customer explicitly permits hashed PII fields; default is hash+salt per-tenant.

Open questions and risks:
- How granular should SAI be for extremely dynamic grants (short-lived feature flags)? Risk of index thrash. Proposed mitigation: do not index sub-minute grants; use graph evaluation for those.
- SIEM cost amplification: sending evidence_refs plus required enrichment may increase event size. Recommend enabling sampling and compression at adaptor.
- Legal holds: how to manage evidence immutability for legal discovery? Need legal sign-off for retention policy and object-lock configuration.

Next actions and owners:
- SEC team to finalize SAI entry schema and sign-off KMS usage (owner: Priya) - due 2026-03-24.
- Infra to prototype fast verifier endpoint and indexer idempotency (owner: Alex Chen) - due 2026-03-31.
- SRE to build SAI health dashboard prototype (owner: Samantha Li) - due 2026-04-07.

Appendix: quick checklist for a safe rollback during canary
- Flip feature-flag to 'legacy-graph' for affected orgs (immediate).
- Mark the last index_version as deprecated and alert indexer to stop writes to that tenant.
- Run discrepancy export for 24 hours and store in audit-archive for postmortem.
- Rehydrate any missing evidence bundles from backup and notify security ops.

End of document.
